You are writing a concrete EXECUTION PLAN for a secondary-income business for Hooman (Adobe eng manager; $25-150K capital; ~10-20 hrs/wk alongside a day job; wants $5-30K/mo; already building CutLog).

IDEA: "Buy a cash-flowing boring B2B / vertical micro-SaaS ($2-8K MRR, $80-150K)"

The deep-research/validation stage produced these findings (JSON) — BUILD THE PLAN AROUND THE VALIDATED REALITY, not the original optimistic pitch:
{
  "idea": "Buy a cash-flowing boring B2B / vertical micro-SaaS ($2-8K MRR, $80-150K all-cash) and operate/improve it as a secondary income stream",
  "slug": "buy_microsaas",
  "assumptions_checked": [
    {
      "claim": "Empire Flippers / small-SaaS listings trade at ~25-40x monthly multiple",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "The cited EF listing (#94153) was 32x monthly but DISTRESSED (profit -50%, rev -37% YoY). Market median is higher: Acquire.com reports SaaS sold at median 3.9x ANNUAL profit (~47x monthly) in both 2024 and 2025 (blog.acquire.com biannual report); FE International 5-7x annual SDE for sub-$2M SaaS; Aventis 4.7x EV/revenue. 25-40x monthly (~2.1-3.3x annual) only holds for the tiny sub-$150K, founder-dependent tier Hooman shops in — and that low multiple is a RISK discount, not a bargain."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Empire Flippers has transacted $589M+ across 2,639+ businesses; marketplaces are real and at scale",
      "status": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "EF about page states '$580M+ worth of online businesses' (mid-update from $450M); consistent. Acquire.com independently: $500M+ closed volume, 2,000+ startups sold, 500K+ entrepreneurs, $2B+ verified buyer funds (acquire.com/). Strongest part of the pitch."
    },
    {
      "claim": "An $80-150K all-cash deal buys $3-6K/mo net at purchase",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "At realistic low-tier ~35x monthly, $80-150K buys ~$2.3-4.3K/mo net, not $3-6K. To net $3-6K you'd pay $105-210K. Pitch entry income nudged DOWN to ~$2-4K/mo. Supply of listings this size is abundant; quality is the constraint."
    },
    {
      "claim": "$3-6K/mo grows to $8-15K/mo over 12-24 months",
      "status": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Survivorship-optimistic. Requires sustained 4-8%/mo growth; but small SaaS is sold BECAUSE the founder stalled (flat/declining). Avg B2B SaaS churn ~3.5%/mo (wearefounders.uk/shno.co); new owners typically see a churn spike + revenue DIP in months 1-6. Base case is hold-flat to modest lift; $8-15K is a top-quartile, actively-operated outcome, not expected."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Downside is capped at the all-cash purchase price",
      "status": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "All-cash, no SBA/PG/home-lien means max loss = the $80-150K minus resale value — materially safer than the SBA-leveraged physical buys in the same report. Genuine cap ONLY holds with escrow + source-verified revenue + earnout/seller note; without those the effective downside is worse."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Hooman's engineering brain is a real diligence + AI-ops edge",
      "status": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Most micro-SaaS buyers are non-technical flippers/operators. An Adobe infra engineer can read code/infra to catch tech debt and single-points-of-failure in diligence, and cut hosting cost + ship AI/features post-close. Uncommon, defensible edge — his single best reason to prefer BUY."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Seller financing is a norm he can lean on to reduce cash outlay",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "'75-90% of small business acquisitions under $5M use seller financing' is a MAIN STREET/SBA stat (thedealsheet.co). Empire Flippers explicitly says 'cash upfront remains the most popular option' for digital deals (EF financing page). Notes/earnouts are negotiable (esp. with motivated sellers) but NOT the default in digital — budget mostly cash."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Buying beats building because ~5% of built micro-SaaS reach $5-20K/mo (distribution is the gap)",
      "status": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "SaaSRanger (1,000+ founders): only ~18% 'make it' at all; revenue tiers imply ~5% reach $5-20K/mo. For a founder whose only weakness is distribution, acquiring an already-distributing business is the rational move — the pitch's core strategic logic holds."
    }
  ],
  "competitors": [
    "Acquire.com (MicroAcquire) — 500K+ entrepreneurs, $2B+ buyer funds, 2,000+ sold; highest volume in the $80-150K band",
    "Empire Flippers — $580M+ transacted, most vetted listings (also priced highest)",
    "Flippa — highest volume, most junk, heaviest diligence burden",
    "FE International — broker for larger/cleaner SaaS (5-10x annual SDE tier)",
    "Micro-PE / holdco aggregators competing to acquire: SureSwift Capital, Tiny (Tiny Capital), XO Capital, Dura Software, plus dozens of cash-ready solo portfolio buyers — these outbid a slower solo buyer on clean assets",
    "Product-market incumbents in whatever vertical he buys into (e.g. Toast in restaurants, entrenched dental PMS, etc.) — vertical SaaS is a ~$94.86B market with an entrenched leader per niche"
  ],
  "economics_verified": "Entry: $80-150K all-cash buys ~$2-4K/mo verified net (NOT $3-6K) at realistic low-tier ~30-42x monthly (~3-3.5x annual SDE). That low multiple is a risk discount, not a bargain — market median for quality SaaS is ~3.9-4.7x annual. Cash yield at entry ~20-35%/yr before growth. 24-month outcome: base case flat-to-$3-5K/mo (churn spike + dip likely in months 1-6); upside $6-10K/mo only if he actively operates and rerates a messy deal; $8-15K is top-quartile, not expected. Downside genuinely capped at $80-150K (no PG) ONLY with escrow + source-verified revenue + earnout/seller note. Time: 10-20 hrs/wk, front-loaded (more in months 1-6), delegable to a VA/contractor dev only after absorption. KEY CHANGES vs pitch: entry income $3-6K→$2-4K; 24mo $8-15K→base $3-5K/upside $6-10K; financing 'available'→budget mostly cash; reframed from growth-double to durable-cash-yield purchase.",
  "verdict": "CONDITIONAL",
  "confidence": "MEDIUM",
  "kill_risks": [
    "Buying a melting ice cube — small SaaS is sold because the founder stalled; many quietly decline, so a post-close churn spike means overpaying for a shrinking annuity",
    "Fake/inflated metrics — screenshot P&Ls, one-time revenue dressed as recurring, churn masked by new logos; mitigated only by read-only Stripe/bank access + cohort retention + escrow",
    "Founder/key-person dependency — the real 'product' is often undocumented ops and support relationships that don't transfer",
    "Platform/disintermediation risk — single-platform apps (Shopify/WP/Stripe add-ons) or thin wrappers an AI feature can absorb have no moat",
    "Adverse selection in bidding wars — cash-ready micro-PE outbids a slow solo buyer on clean assets, leaving the messy deals (fine only where his eng edge fixes them, a trap where messiness is legal/customer/market)",
    "Time is the true constraint — sold as 'capital not time' but months 1-6 are real work while CutLog is also in its 0-1 grind; a neglected acquisition churns out",
    "Concentration — one $150K deal is all eggs in one basket; a single diligence miss loses the whole allocation"
  ],
  "best_niche_or_target": "A flat-but-sticky vertical B2B system-of-record / workflow micro-SaaS in an unglamorous trade (field-service, specialty-trade POS, niche compliance/recordkeeping, dental/med-lab ops), ~$2-4K/mo SOURCE-VERIFIED net, ≥18-24mo history, <20% single-customer concentration, current owner <10 hrs/wk, bought at ~3-3.5x annual SDE all-cash with a 10-30% earnout/seller note + escrow + non-compete + 60-90d transition. His specific edge lane: a TECHNICALLY MESSY, fixable deal (ugly code / high hosting cost / burned-out solo founder) that non-technical buyers discount and he rerates — sourced on Empire Flippers or Acquire.com, or via direct outreach to founders of stalled niche tools. Explicitly reject: consumer apps, SEO content, Chrome extensions, and any platform-dependent single-app whose host can kill it.",
  "_idea": {
    "slug": "buy_microsaas",
    "name": "Buy a cash-flowing boring B2B / vertical micro-SaaS ($2-8K MRR, $80-150K)",
    "claims": "Skips the 0->1 distribution grind by buying customers; $3-6K/mo net at purchase -> $8-15K/mo over 12-24mo; downside capped at all-cash price; Hooman eng brain = diligence + AI-ops edge. Proof cited: Empire Flippers listings ~25-40x monthly multiple, $589M+ transacted. Key open questions: real current multiples for $2-8K MRR SaaS? realistic post-acquisition churn/growth? how much operating time really required? seller-financing norms?"
  }
}

Also read your own research doc at /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/trackB/deep/buy_microsaas/01_research_validation.md for detail.

Write a concrete, realistic execution plan:
  - The specific target (exact niche/exam/tool/vertical/acquisition profile chosen in research).
  - First 90 days: week-by-week concrete actions, who does what, what gets validated when.
  - Months 4-12: path to the revenue target, hiring/delegation plan (this MUST stay part-time for Hooman).
  - Itemized budget within $25-150K; monthly burn; break-even point.
  - Revenue model + realistic ramp curve (subscribers/clients/deals over time).
  - Concrete go/no-go decision gates and the cheapest possible validation BEFORE committing real money.
  - How it coexists with CutLog for Hooman's limited hours (capital+delegation vs focus).

WRITE the plan to /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/trackB/deep/buy_microsaas/02_execution_plan.md (use Write). Return a ~200-word summary of the plan as your final text.

1	# Deep Research + Validation — "Buy a cash-flowing boring B2B / vertical micro-SaaS"
2	
3	**Idea slug**: `buy_microsaas`
4	**Date**: 2026-07-01. **Analyst**: Claude (Opus 4.8), skeptic pass.
5	**Source pitch**: `runs/trackB/TRACKB_REPORT.md` §4 pick #4 (scored 7.85) and the "acquire
6	proven $8-12K/mo vertical micro-SaaS" variant (#9, 7.75).
7	
8	**Pitch in one line**: Instead of building 0→1, *buy* a small cash-flowing B2B/vertical
9	SaaS for $80-150K all-cash. Inherit the customers (Hooman's distribution gap). Net $3-6K/mo
10	at purchase → $8-15K/mo over 12-24mo. Downside capped at the all-cash price. Hooman's
11	engineering brain = a diligence + AI-ops edge.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. Claim-by-claim verification
16	
17	### Claim A — "Empire Flippers listings trade at ~25-40x monthly multiple"
18	**Verdict: PARTIALLY-TRUE (and the framing is misleading).**
19	
20	- The one live EF SaaS listing cited (#94153) was **32x monthly** — but that business was
21	  **distressed**: profit down 50%, revenue down 37% YoY. 32x on a declining business is a
22	  *low* multiple that reflects the decline, not a healthy benchmark.
23	  (Source: empireflippers.com/marketplace/, fetched 2026-07-01.)
24	- "25-40x monthly" = **~2.1x-3.3x annual profit**. That is at or **below** the true market
25	  median. Acquire.com's biannual report: **SaaS sold at a median 3.9x annual profit multiple
26	  in BOTH 2024 and 2025 (low-to-mid 4x average)** — i.e. **~47x monthly**, not 25-40x.
27	  (Source: blog.acquire.com/acquire-com-biannual-acquisition-multiples-report-jan-2026/)
28	- FE International: SaaS "typically 4x-10x annual SDE"; **5.0-7.0x for businesses under $2M**,
29	  7-10x above. (Source: feinternational.com/blog/saas-metrics-value-saas-business/)
30	- Aventis Advisors: 500+ private SaaS transactions 2015-2025, median **4.7x EV/Revenue**
31	  (revenue, not profit — a different basis). (Source: aventis-advisors.com/saas-valuation-multiples/)
32	
33	**So which is right?** The apparent contradiction resolves by deal SIZE:
34	- Larger/higher-quality SaaS ($250K+, clean metrics) → 4-7x annual (40-70x monthly).
35	- **Tiny sub-$150K, single-founder, plugin/app-tier SaaS → genuinely lower**, often 2.5-3.5x
36	  annual (30-42x monthly). This is the *only* band where "25-40x monthly" holds — precisely
37	  the band Hooman is shopping in. So the pitch's multiple is roughly right *for the low tier*,
38	  but the reason is not "cheap deals" — it's that small SaaS is riskier (founder-dependent,
39	  thin moat, higher churn), and the discount is compensation for that risk. **The low multiple
40	  is a warning label, not a bargain.**
41	
42	### Claim B — "Empire Flippers: 2,639+ businesses sold, $589M+ transacted"
43	**Verdict: VERIFIED.** EF's own about page now states "**over $580M+ worth of online
44	businesses**" (an earlier line said $450M; the site is mid-update). The $589M/2,639 figures
45	are consistent with EF's public cadence and are legitimate.
46	(Source: empireflippers.com/about-us/) Acquire.com independently: **$500M+ closed volume,
47	2,000+ startups sold, 500K+ entrepreneurs, $2B+ verified buyer funds.** (Source: acquire.com/)
48	**The marketplaces are real and at scale.** This claim is the strongest part of the pitch.
49	
50	### Claim C — "Net $3-6K/mo at purchase for an $80-150K all-cash deal"
51	**Verdict: VERIFIED (arithmetic) but note the tension with Claim A.**
52	- At the *low-tier* 30-42x monthly multiple: $80-150K ÷ 35x ≈ **$2.3-4.3K/mo net**. To get
53	  $3-6K/mo you'd pay $105-210K at 35x. So $80-150K buys you roughly **$2-4K/mo net**, not
54	  $3-6K, at realistic small-tier multiples. **Pitch number nudged down.**
55	- Businesses this small that DO exist for sale at these prices are abundant (thousands on
56	  Flippa/Acquire), so **supply is not the constraint** — quality is.
57	
58	### Claim D — "$3-6K/mo → $8-15K/mo over 12-24 months"
59	**Verdict: UNVERIFIED / OPTIMISTIC (survivorship bias).**
60	- Doubling-to-tripling net profit in 12-24mo requires **sustained 4-8%/mo growth**. UnlockSaaS
61	  benchmark: indie SaaS at the $1-10K stage grows **5-15%/mo** *when growing at all* — but
62	  that is conditional on the business still being on a growth path. **Most acquired micro-SaaS
63	  are bought precisely because the founder stalled/lost interest — i.e. flat or declining.**
64	- Post-acquisition reality cuts the other way first: average B2B SaaS churn is **~3.5%/mo**
65	  (2.6% voluntary + 0.8% involuntary). (Source: wearefounders.uk / shno.co churn benchmarks.)
66	  A new owner with no relationship to customers, mid-migration, typically sees a **churn spike
67	  and a revenue dip in months 1-6**, not immediate growth. The pitch's "→ $8-15K" ignores the
68	  near-certain initial dip and assumes the buyer both stops the bleed AND re-accelerates.
69	- **Reframe**: realistic base case is *hold flat / modest 10-30% lift* over 24mo, with the
70	  upside case ($8-15K) being a top-quartile outcome contingent on Hooman actively operating
71	  (see time claim). Treat the growth story as optional upside, price the deal on trailing cash.
72	
73	### Claim E — "Downside capped at the all-cash purchase price"
74	**Verdict: VERIFIED — and this is genuinely the idea's best feature.**
75	- All-cash, no SBA, no personal guarantee, no home lien → **max loss = the $80-150K** (minus
76	  any residual resale value). This is materially safer than the SBA-leveraged physical buys
77	  (self-storage/laundromat) in the same report, where a PG can exceed the cash in.
78	- Caveat: deals do fall through and metrics get faked; the "cap" only holds if he uses **escrow
79	  + source-verified revenue (Stripe/bank login, not screenshots) + an earnout/seller note** so
80	  part of the price is contingent. Without those, the effective downside is worse than "the price."
81	
82	### Claim F — "Hooman's engineering brain = a diligence + AI-ops edge"
83	**Verdict: VERIFIED (real, and rare in this buyer pool).**
84	- Most micro-SaaS buyers are non-technical operators/portfolio flippers. An Adobe infra
85	  engineer can (a) read the codebase and infra to spot tech debt / scaling landmines /
86	  single-points-of-failure that non-tech buyers miss in diligence, and (b) cut hosting/ops
87	  cost and ship features/AI automation post-close. This is a **legitimate, uncommon edge** and
88	  the single most defensible reason *this* buyer should consider *this* shape.
89	
90	### Claim G — "Seller financing is a norm he can lean on"
91	**Verdict: PARTIALLY-TRUE — true for Main Street, much weaker in digital.**
92	- "Seller financing powers **75-90% of small business acquisitions under $5M**" — but that
93	  statistic is for **traditional/SBA Main Street** deals. (Source: thedealsheet.co)
94	- **Empire Flippers explicitly says "cash upfront remains the most popular option"** on their
95	  digital marketplace. (Source: empireflippers.com/oba/online-business-financing/) In digital
96	  SaaS deals, seller notes/earnouts happen but are **not** the default; motivated/declining-
97	  business sellers are more open to them. So Hooman *can* negotiate a note/earnout (and should,
98	  as a risk-shifter), but should NOT assume he'll routinely finance most of the price. **Budget
99	  to pay mostly cash.**
100	
101	### Claim H (implicit) — "Buying beats building because ~5% of built micro-SaaS reach $5-20K/mo"
102	**Verdict: VERIFIED (this is the strongest strategic argument for the idea).**
103	- SaaSRanger (1,000+ founders): only **~18% "make it"** at all, and the report's revenue tiers
104	  imply only ~5% reach $5-20K/mo, ~2% reach $20-50K/mo. (Source: SaaSRanger "Micro-SaaS
105	  Revenue Reality," via search.) Famous fast ramps had pre-built audiences. **For a founder
106	  whose ONLY gap is distribution, buying an already-distributing business is the rational move.**
107	
108	---
109	
110	## 2. Competitors / the market Hooman is buying INTO
111	
112	Two competitive layers matter:
113	
114	**(a) Competition to ACQUIRE (the buy-side auction).** Hooman is bidding against a professional
115	buyer pool that has grown enormously:
116	- **Acquire.com**: 500K+ entrepreneurs, **$2B+ in verified buyer funds** chasing 2,000+
117	  lifetime sales. Demand >> supply of *clean* small SaaS → good assets get bid up / go fast
118	  (avg **81 days on market**, most sub-$250K deals close **within 90 days**).
119	  (Source: blog.acquire.com report.)
120	- **Empire Flippers, Flippa, FE International, MicroAcquire/Acquire** — the marketplaces.
121	- **Micro-PE / holdco aggregators**: SureSwift Capital, Tiny (Tiny Capital), XO Capital,
122	  Dura Software, Fastlane (Andrew Gazdecki-adjacent), plus dozens of solo "portfolio" buyers.
123	  These are faster, cash-ready, and often waive diligence Hooman can't. **He will lose bidding
124	  wars on the obviously-good listings.** His edge is finding the *technically messy* deal others
125	  fear — which is exactly where his eng diligence pays off.
126	
127	**(b) Competition the ACQUIRED business faces (product-market).** A "boring vertical B2B"
128	tool's competitors are the incumbents/OEMs this project keeps flagging: vertical SaaS is a
129	**$94.86B market** but each niche has an entrenched leader (e.g. Toast in restaurants, dental

132	vendor (Shopify/WordPress/Stripe) could absorb — that's the disintermediation risk the report

# Execution Plan — Buy a Cash-Flowing Boring B2B / Vertical Micro-SaaS

**Owner**: Hooman Shariati. **Written**: 2026-07-01 by Claude (Opus 4.8).
**Companion docs**: `01_research_validation.md` (the skeptic pass this plan is built on).
**Verdict this plan implements**: CONDITIONAL / MEDIUM confidence. This is a
**~20-35% cash-on-cash yield capital deployment with a capped downside**, NOT a
"double it in 24 months" growth play. Everything below underwrites on **trailing,
source-verified cash flow with ZERO value assigned to the growth story.**

---

## 0. TL;DR — what this actually is

Deploy **$80-150K all-cash** to buy ONE vertical-B2B system-of-record micro-SaaS doing
**$2-4K/mo source-verified net**, priced at **~3.0-3.5x annual SDE (30-42x monthly)**,
with **escrow + a 10-30% earnout/seller note + non-compete + 60-90d transition**. Operate
it part-time (10-20 hrs/wk, front-loaded to months 1-6), stop the churn, cut hosting cost,
ship 1-2 AI/feature wins, then **delegate to a VA + contractor dev** so it settles into a
low-touch cash stream. Realistic 24-mo target: **hold-flat-to-$3-5K/mo base case; $6-10K/mo
upside only if he actively rerates a messy deal.** The whole thesis rests on Hooman's rare
edge: he can read the code others can't, so he buys the **technically-messy-but-fixable**
deal the non-technical buyer pool discounts.

**This coexists with CutLog because it spends CAPITAL + DELEGATION, not CutLog's building
hours — EXCEPT months 1-6, which are genuinely hands-on. See §8. Do not close a deal in a
month where CutLog needs his full attention.**

---

## 1. The Specific Target (locked)

**Acquisition profile — all criteria are filters, not preferences:**

| Dimension | Hard filter |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Vertical B2B **system-of-record / workflow tool** in an unglamorous trade: field-service ops, specialty-trade POS/quoting, niche compliance & recordkeeping, dental/med-lab ops, property/HOA admin, trade-specific scheduling. |
| **Revenue** | ≥18-24 mo history; B2B; **annual or sticky monthly** billing; **source-verified via read-only Stripe + bank**, never screenshots. |
| **Net (SDE)** | **$2-4K/mo trailing** (do NOT stretch to $6K; that costs $105-210K and breaks the budget). |
| **Price / multiple** | **$80-150K all-cash; 3.0-3.5x annual SDE (30-42x monthly).** Pay the low end for anything with declining or flat-fragile revenue. |
| **Churn** | Logo churn ≤ ~3%/mo, **cohort retention curve flattens** (not masked by new-logo adds). |
| **Concentration** | **<20% revenue from any single customer.** |
| **Owner load** | Current owner works **<10 hrs/wk** (proves part-time operability). |
| **Moat** | Switching cost from being a system-of-record. **REJECT**: consumer apps, SEO/content sites, Chrome extensions, thin AI wrappers, and any single-platform app (Shopify/WP/Stripe add-on) whose host can kill it. |
| **The edge lane** | Prefer a deal that is **technically messy but fixable** — ugly code, high hosting bill, burned-out solo founder — that non-technical buyers discount and Hooman can rerate. That is the ONE place his engineering edge converts to alpha. |
| **Deal structure** | Escrow + **10-30% held as 6-12mo earnout/seller note** + non-compete + **60-90d seller transition + SOP handover**. |

**Where to source**: Empire Flippers (most vetted, priced highest), Acquire.com (most
volume in this band), Flippa (most volume, most junk, heaviest diligence), + **direct
outreach to founders of stalled niche tools** (best price, no auction — the highest-alpha
channel once he knows his niche).

**Pick a lane before shopping.** Hooman should choose **1-2 verticals he can underwrite
credibly** (e.g. field-service + one compliance/recordkeeping niche) so he becomes a fast,
confident buyer instead of a tourist. Domain familiarity = faster diligence = wins the
messy deals others can't judge.

---

## 2. First 90 Days (week-by-week)

**Phase A (Weeks 1-4): Setup + deal-flow, ~zero money spent.**

- **Wk 1** — Hooman: open buyer accounts on Empire Flippers, Acquire.com, Flippa. Set
  saved-search alerts for the profile in §1 ($75-160K, SaaS, B2B). Pick the 1-2 target
  verticals. Write a one-page personal Buy Box (this §1 as a checklist).
- **Wk 2** — Build the **diligence toolkit** (reusable, this is his moat as a repeat buyer):
  a spreadsheet model (trailing SDE, cohort retention, concentration, churn, hosting cost);
  a code/infra red-flag checklist (single points of failure, secrets in repo, backup story,
  dependency rot, scaling cost); a standard **read-only-access request** template (Stripe,
  bank/PayPal, Google Analytics, hosting console, repo).
- **Wk 3** — Review **20-30 listings** against the Buy Box. Reject fast. Goal: a shortlist
  of **5-8** that pass the paper screen. Log every rejection reason (builds pattern memory).
- **Wk 4** — Request seller intros / LOI-precursor calls on the top **3-5**. Ask the killer
  questions: why selling, owner hrs/wk, top-5 customer % of revenue, tech stack, who does
  support, what breaks at 2x scale.

**Phase B (Weeks 5-8): Deep diligence on 1-2 finalists (cheap validation — see §6).**

- **Wk 5** — Sign NDA; get **read-only Stripe + bank + analytics** on the #1 finalist.
  Reconcile bank deposits ↔ Stripe MRR ↔ the P&L they showed. **If they refuse live
  read-only access → walk.** (Kill-risk #2.)
- **Wk 6** — Build the real cohort-retention curve from Stripe data. Confirm churn, MRR
  trend (flat/growing, not decline dressed up by new logos), concentration <20%.
- **Wk 7** — **Technical diligence (Hooman's edge)**: read the codebase, map infra, price
  the true hosting/ops cost, list the tech debt and the 1-2 quick wins (hosting cut, an AI
  feature). This is where he decides "messy-but-fixable" vs "messy-and-a-trap."
- **Wk 8** — Underwrite on trailing SDE only (zero growth credit). If it pencils at
  3.0-3.5x with a capped downside → submit **LOI** with escrow + 10-30% earnout/note +
  non-compete + 60-90d transition. **GATE 3 (§6) here.**

**Phase C (Weeks 9-13): Close + start transition.**

- **Wk 9-10** — Confirmatory diligence during escrow; legal review of the asset-purchase
  agreement (budget a lawyer, §5). Lock the transition plan + SOP handover in the contract.
- **Wk 11** — **Close.** Funds via escrow; earnout/note documented. Migrate access,
  domains, Stripe, hosting, repo to Hooman.
- **Wk 12-13** — Absorb: shadow the seller on support, read every open ticket, do NOT
  change pricing or product yet. Goal for months 1-2 is **stop the churn / do no harm**,
  not grow. Ship only the safest cost win (e.g. hosting rightsizing) once stable.

**If no deal clears diligence by Week 13 → that's a SUCCESS, not a failure.** Keep the
alerts running and repeat Phase A/B on new listings. **Never force a deal to hit a
deadline** — patience is the whole risk-management strategy here.

---

## 3. Months 4-12 — Path to the revenue target (stays part-time)

**Operating cadence shifts from "learn it" to "stabilize + modest lift + delegate."**

- **Months 4-6 — Stabilize & instrument.** Kill involuntary churn (dunning/failed-card
  recovery — usually a free 10-20% MRR recovery). Fix the worst tech debt. Ship **one**
  customer-visible win (an AI feature or a top-requested feature). Write SOPs for support
  and ops as he goes. Time: still **~15 hrs/wk**.
- **Months 7-9 — Delegate.** Hire a **part-time VA / support contractor** (front-line
  support, onboarding, mundane ops) and put a **fractional contractor dev** on retainer for
  the tech debt / feature backlog. Hooman moves to **owner/operator: 5-10 hrs/wk** —
  strategy, roadmap, key-account touch, reviewing the dev's work.
- **Months 10-12 — Optional lift.** Test a 5-10% price increase on new/renewing customers
  (system-of-record = low elasticity). One low-effort acquisition channel already used by
  the business (e.g. its existing SEO/referral). Reassess: hold, reinvest, or add a 2nd
  asset.

**Realistic revenue path (base case, priced this way on purpose):**

| Month | Net/mo | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (close) | $2-4K | Entry, source-verified |
| 1-3 | $1.8-3.6K | Expected transition churn dip |
| 4-6 | $2-4K | Recover to entry via dunning + retention |
| 7-12 | $2.5-5K | Modest lift; delegation frees Hooman |
| 24 (base) | $3-5K | Durable; **upside $6-10K** only if he actively rerates a messy deal |

**$8-15K/mo is a top-quartile, actively-operated outcome — do NOT plan on it or pay for
it.** The plan succeeds if the asset holds $3-5K/mo net at 5-10 hrs/wk — that is a durable
20-35% cash yield plus optionality.

---

## 4. Delegation / hiring plan (must stay part-time)

- **Months 1-6**: Hooman + the **seller (paid transition/consulting)**. No hires yet — he
  must understand the business before delegating it.
- **Month 7+**: **VA / support contractor** ($800-1,500/mo) for front-line support & ops.
- **Month 7+ (as needed)**: **fractional contractor dev** on retainer or per-task ($1-3K/mo
  variable) for the backlog. Hooman never becomes the full-time dev — he directs.
- **End state**: Hooman at **5-10 hrs/wk** (roadmap, key accounts, reviewing contractors).
  If it can't get to <10 hrs/wk, it's either the wrong asset or needs more delegation budget.

---

## 5. Budget (within $25-150K), burn, break-even

**One-time acquisition + close (from the capital allocation):**

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Purchase price (mostly cash; 10-30% as earnout/note) | **$80-150K** |
| Escrow fee (~0.5-1% of price) | $500-1,500 |
| Legal review of APA | $2-5K |
| Diligence tooling / paid data | ~$500 |
| **Working-capital reserve** (transition dip + first hires + surprises) | **$10-15K** |
| **Total capital committed** | **~$95-170K** — *aim for the $80-120K purchase band to stay inside $150K all-in.* |

**To respect the $150K ceiling: target a purchase price of ~$80-120K**, leaving room for
close costs + the $10-15K reserve. A $150K purchase blows past the budget once costs and
reserve are added.

**Ongoing monthly burn (post-close):**

- Months 1-6: hosting + tools **$300-1,000/mo**; seller transition consulting (often
  bundled into price or a few $K one-time). Effectively **< $1K/mo** cash burn.
- Months 7+: + VA **$800-1,500/mo** + contractor dev **$1-3K/mo variable** = **$2-4.5K/mo**.

**Break-even / payback:**
- The business is **cash-flow positive from day one** (that's the point — you buy profit).
- **Payback of purchase price**: at $2-4K/mo net, **~3-4 years** to return capital (20-35%
  annual cash yield), FASTER if he rerates it, plus the resale value of the asset itself
  (which can return most of the capital at exit). This is a yield + optionality play, not a
  quick flip.

---

## 6. Go/No-Go gates + cheapest validation BEFORE real money

**All validation up to LOI costs ~$0 and only Hooman's hours. Do NOT wire money until
Gate 3.**

- **GATE 0 — Personal fit (Week 0, free).** Can Hooman honestly commit **15-20 hrs/wk for
  months 1-6** alongside CutLog? If CutLog is mid-crunch, **defer the whole thing** — do not
  split the hours the CutLog thesis needs. This is a scheduling decision, not a deal
  decision.
- **GATE 1 — Paper screen (Weeks 3-4, free).** Passes the §1 Buy Box on the listing's
  stated numbers + vertical fit. Reject 90%+ here.
- **GATE 2 — Source-verified metrics (Weeks 5-6, free).** **Live read-only Stripe + bank
  reconcile to the claimed P&L**; cohort retention flat/growing; concentration <20%. Seller
  refuses live access → **instant walk.** This single gate kills kill-risks #1 and #2.
- **GATE 3 — Underwrites on trailing cash + tech is fixable (Weeks 7-8, free).** Pencils at
  3.0-3.5x annual SDE with **zero growth credit**; Hooman's code/infra review says
  "messy-but-fixable" not "trap." Only now submit LOI with escrow + earnout/note +
  non-compete + transition.
- **GATE 4 — Confirmatory diligence in escrow (Weeks 9-10).** No surprises; contract has the
  risk-shifters. Any material discrepancy → walk (escrow protects the money).

**Cheapest validation of the whole STRATEGY before committing to any deal:** run Phases A-B
on **2-3 real listings as a dry run** — request read-only access, build the model, do the
tech review — and only proceed to LOI if a real one clears Gate 3. If nothing clears after
~2-3 months of looking, that's strong signal the clean-deal supply/price doesn't work for
him, and he keeps the capital.

---

## 7. Kill-risks → mitigations (carry-through from research)

1. **Melting ice cube** → underwrite trailing only; ≥18-24mo verified flat/growing; earnout; walk from declines.
2. **Fake metrics** → live read-only Stripe/bank; cohort retention; escrow. No live access = no deal.
3. **Key-person dependency** → 60-90d transition + non-compete + SOP handover in the contract.
4. **Platform / disintermediation** → buy system-of-record with switching cost; reject platform add-ons and thin AI wrappers.
5. **Bidding-war adverse selection** → deliberately fish the messy-but-fixable pond his eng edge wins; walk from messy-in-ways-he-can't-fix (legal/customer/market).
6. **Time is the real constraint** → Gate 0; front-load hours to months 1-6; delegate hard by month 7; never neglect it (neglect → churn).
7. **Concentration (one deal = all eggs)** → accept single-asset risk at this capital level; only add a 2nd asset after the 1st is delegated and stable.

---

## 8. Coexistence with CutLog (the binding real-world constraint)

**CutLog is the primary bet and needs Hooman's scarce BUILDING hours (0→1 grind). This
acquisition is deliberately chosen because it consumes CAPITAL + DELEGATION instead —
EXCEPT the months 1-6 absorption, which is genuinely hands-on.**

Rules to keep both alive:
1. **Sequence, don't stack the crunches.** Do NOT close a micro-SaaS deal in a month where
   CutLog needs a launch push. The deal-flow (Phase A) is passive/async and can run
   continuously in the background; only pull the trigger (Phase B/C) when CutLog has slack.
2. **Front-load then delegate.** Absorb in months 1-6, then hand support to a VA and dev to
   a contractor by month 7 so it drops to 5-10 hrs/wk and stops competing with CutLog.
3. **Capital is separate from attention.** The $80-120K is money Hooman can commit without
   spending building hours; that's the strategic reason BUY beats BUILD for a *second*
   stream (his only gap is distribution, and he's buying distribution).
4. **Hard stop**: if at Gate 0 he can't spare 15-20 hrs/wk for 6 months without hurting
   CutLog, **defer the acquisition entirely** rather than split focus. A neglected
   acquisition churns out and loses the allocation (kill-risk #6).

---

## 9. Immediate next actions

1. **Hooman**: answer Gate 0 — can he give this 15-20 hrs/wk for months 1-6 without hurting
   CutLog, and in which calendar window? (Scope confirmation before any spend.)
2. **Hooman**: pick the 1-2 target verticals he can underwrite credibly.
3. Then: open marketplace accounts + saved searches, build the diligence toolkit, start the
   Phase-A dry run on 2-3 real listings — all free, all reversible.
